summary: Telegram bot library: static patterns flagged, semantic verification inconclusive
details: node-telegram-sockets is a Telegram Bot API client library. Static keyword co-occurrence rules fired on lib/telegram.js, src/telegram.js, and lib/telegramWebHook.js due to the joint presence of HTTP/HTTPS imports, fs.readFileSync, and the substring 'ping' within the same files. The 'ping' matches correspond to the Telegram bot 'ping' command/method handling, which is part of the legitimate Bot API surface, not an OS ping command for host reconnaissance. The fs.readFileSync calls in the webhook module are consistent with loading TLS certificate/key files required to host an HTTPS webhook endpoint for Telegram. No specific hardcoded non-first-party exfiltration destination, no credential-path read (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser stores), no lifecycle script, and no install-time fetch-and-execute is evident from the static evidence alone. Stage findings did not parse, so traced corroboration of intent is not available; the structural shape is that of a Telegram bot library, not a credential stealer, but a human reviewer should confirm the webhook handler is not relaying caller data to an undeclared destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
